L0@P0: The new lantibiotic nukacin producers, strain ISK-1
L1@P0: previously labeled as Pediococcus sp. ISK-1 and
L2@P0: strain Nagano, were characterized biochemically and
L3@P0: genetically. Cells were spherical, 0.6 µm in size, and
L4@P0: occurred in pairs. The strains were gram-positive,
L5@P0: catalase positive and produced more than 75% of DLlactic acid from glucose and their growth was stimulated by mevalonic acid. The strains tolerated 18%
L6@P0: NaCl. GC content was 36%. 16S rRNA homology revealed that the strains resembled Staphylococcus
L7@P0: warneri. Both strains were confirmed by quantitative
L8@P0: DNA-DNA hybridization to be variant strains of S.
L9@P0: warneri. These strains have been deposited in the
L10@P0: Japan Collection of Microorganism as S. warneri JCM
L11@P0: 10004 for strain ISK-1 and S. warneri JCM 10005 for
L12@P0: strain Nagano.
L13@P0: In the northern Kyushu area, many old aged
L14@P0: Nukadoko (bed of fermented rice bran) have been
L15@P0: maintained until now and some are believed to have
L16@P0: lasted for a few hundred years (Kimura et al., 1997).
L17@P0: Nukadoko is usually used for pickle fermentation using
L18@P0: washed vegetables without any aseptic treatment. We
L19@P0: therefore suspected that Nukadoko must possess a
L20@P0: native microflora control system that attacks undesirable microorganisms that comes into contact with the
L21@P0: bed from the environment. We isolated two organisms,
L22@P0: strain ISK-1 and strain Nagano, from an old aged bed
L23@P0: owned by Mrs. Sato in Kitakyushu-shi, Japan, a cooking instructor for Iwashino-Nukamisodaki which is a
L24@P0: local traditional Japanese cuisine, consisting of cooked
L25@P0: sardine with old aged Nukadoko. These strains were
L26@P0: isolated by the following procedure. One gram of
L27@P0: Nukadoko was suspended in 10 ml of pure water and
L28@P0: stood for 24 h at 30°C. One milliliter of the suspension
L29@P0: was suspended in 100 ml of thioglycolate (TGC, Difco
L30@P0: Laboratories, Detroit, MI, USA) with 1.5% agar and
L31@P0: 1.5% CaCO3 to which NaN3 10 ppm and cycloheximide 10 ppm were supplemented. The agar plates
L32@P0: were incubated in an anaerobic jar for 2 days. The organism was purified by repeating single colony isolation on TGC agar plate.
L33@P0: Strain ISK-1 and strain Nagano grew in both anaerobic and microaerophilic conditions. These strains were
L34@P0: gram-positive cocci occurring in pairs, catalase positive, and produced more than 75% of DL-lactic acid
L35@P0: from glucose with only a little amount of acetic acid.
